Change c0481. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): Amidst the wilds of Tartary and Russia, although he still evaded me, I have ever followed in his track.

1818 text: Sometimes the peasants, scared by this horrid apparition, informed me of his path; sometimes he himself, who feared that if I lost all trace I should despair and die, often left some mark to guide me.

1831 text: Sometimes the peasants, scared by this horrid apparition, informed me of his path; sometimes he himself, who feared that if I lost all trace of him, I should despair and die, left some mark to guide me.

Diff: Sometimes the peasants, scared by this horrid apparition, informed me of his path; sometimes he himself, who feared that if I lost all trace {+of him,+} I should despair and die, [-often-] left some mark to guide me.

Context after (unchanged): The snows descended on my head, and I saw the print of his huge step on the white plain.

result.rationale: Removes the adverb 'often' from 'often left some mark to guide me', lessening the sense of Victor's repeated pursuit-tracking by the creature; the added 'of him' is a minor syntactic clarification.
